dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: vihāya nijadehasthaṃ sarvatrāsmīti bhāvayan | dṛḍhena manasā dṛṣṭyā nānyekṣiṇyā sukhī bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 104: GRETIL, Singh and Pradīpaka read nijadehasthaṃ; Wallis prints nijadehasthāṃ. Meaning is the same ('what abides in one's own body').
dharana.rendering: Letting go of what abides in one's own body, contemplating 'I am everywhere' with a firm mind and a gaze that looks at nothing else, one becomes happy.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: the dhāraṇā has a negative side ('I am not my body, nor confined to any place or time') and a positive side ('I am everywhere'). Verse 100 contemplates consciousness in all bodies; here one expands one's own consciousness into all forms. Śivopādhyāya distinguishes the two: here the contemplation is 'all this is myself', the awareness of Sadāśiva or Īśvara. Wallis: 'I am everywhere'.
dharana.instruction: Let go of being located in this body and contemplate steadily, 'I am everywhere.'

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 104 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the habitual location 'here, in this body'
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a self that usually sits in one body, opened out to be present everywhere.
geometry.svg_hint: a small point expanding into a field that fills the whole frame
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Everywhere
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the sense of living only inside this body is released and replaced by 'I am everywhere'. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.secondary: Letting go of being located only in this body

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Letting go of what abides in one's own body, contemplating 'I am everywhere' with a firm mind and a gaze that looks at nothing else, one becomes happy.
adiyogi.method_summary: Let go of the feeling of living only inside this body. With a steady mind and nowhere else to look, contemplate: 'I am everywhere.' Rest in that, and notice the happiness that comes.

honesty.disclosure: Door 081 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 81 (verse 104) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 081 is dharana 81, verse 104. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If this feels disorienting, feel the weight of the body on the floor and open the eyes. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
